summary: Extends the IPFIX flow export protocol and its information model to carry hierarchical structured data and lists of information elements in data records. This allows complex structures such as variable-length lists and containment relationships between templates.

plainLanguage.summary: IPFIX is the protocol routers use to send traffic statistics to a collector. Each record is a flat list of values, which does not fit data that repeats or nests, such as a stack of labels or an alert with several attackers. This RFC adds a way to put a list inside a record, and to say how the items in the list relate to one another.

questions: what is a subtemplatelist in ipfix
subtitle: Carrying lists and nested structures inside IPFIX data records, instead of only single values.

tldr.problem: An IPFIX data record is a flat list of single values, so anything with a repeated or nested structure, such as a stack of MPLS labels or a security alert with several participants, has to be flattened or split across many templates.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds three abstract data types, basicList, subTemplateList and subTemplateMultiList, each with a matching Information Element, plus a set of semantics that say how the elements of a list relate to one another.
tldr.outcome: The extension also changes where the type information lives, since the list type now appears in the data record rather than the template, which means a collector that does not know the extension can still read the rest of the record.

facts.label: Structured data semantics
facts.value: undefined, noneOf, exactlyOneOf, oneOrMoreOf, allOf, ordered

facts.label: Variable length encoding
facts.value: the three-byte length encoding is RECOMMENDED

today: RFC 6313 is a Proposed Standard on the Internet standards track. It updates RFC 5102, and no RFC in the site index obsoletes it. The extension applies to the IPFIX protocol in RFC 5101 and, because PSAMP is built on IPFIX, it applies to packet sampling exports as well.

sections.title: Why IPFIX Needed Structured Data
sections.content:
This document specifies an extension to the IPFIX protocol specification in RFC 5101 and to the IPFIX information model in RFC 5102, to support hierarchical structured data and lists of Information Elements in data records. The extension allows the definition of complex data structures such as variable-length lists and the specification of hierarchical containment relationships between Templates. It also provides the semantics needed to express the relationship among multiple list elements in a structured data record.

The IPFIX protocol gives network administrators access to IP Flow information. The architecture for the export of measured IP Flow information out of an IPFIX Exporting Process to a Collecting Process is defined in the IPFIX architecture, and the information model gives a formal description of IPFIX Information Elements, their name, type and additional semantic information.

The specification applies to the IPFIX protocol specifications, and all of the specifications from RFC 5101 apply unless stated otherwise. Because the PSAMP protocol specifications are based on the IPFIX protocol specifications, the specifications in this document are also valid for the PSAMP protocol. The major difference between the two is that IPFIX exports Flow Records while PSAMP exports Packet Reports; from a pure export point of view a PSAMP export can be seen as a special IPFIX Flow Record containing information about a single packet.
sections.plainLanguage: IPFIX is the protocol routers use to send traffic statistics to a collector. Each record is a flat list of values, which does not fit data that repeats or nests, such as a stack of labels or an alert with several attackers. This RFC adds a way to put a list inside a record, and to say how the items in the list relate to one another.

sections.title: The Limitation of the Flat Data Record
sections.content:
The IPFIX protocol exports information about IP traffic Flows, where a Flow is defined by a set of key attributes such as source and destination IP address and source and destination port. Traffic measurements are exported using a TLV, type, length and value, format. A Template Record is sent once to export the type and length pairs that define the data format, and the Data Records then specify the values for each Flow.

Because of the Template mechanism, IPFIX can export any type of information as long as the relevant Information Element is in the information model, registered with IANA, or specified as an enterprise-specific Information Element. For each Information Element the information model defines a numeric identifier, an abstract data type, an encoding mechanism for the data type and any semantic constraints. Until this extension, only basic, single-valued data types such as numbers, strings and network addresses were supported.

The IPFIX protocol specification does not support the encoding of hierarchical structured data and arbitrary-length lists of Information Elements as fields within a Template Record. As specified, a Data Record is a flat list of single-valued attributes. Yet composing complex hierarchies of data types, with multiple occurrences of each Information Element allowed, is a common data modelling requirement.

The RFC gives the MPLS label stack as the typical example. An early NetFlow implementation used two Information Elements, a label stack entry position followed by a label stack value, and several drawbacks were discovered. The Information Elements in the Template Record had to be imposed so that the position always preceded the value, which interferes with encoding optimizations based on the permutation of Information Element order. And new semantic intelligence, not described in the information model, had to be hard-coded in the Collecting Process, so that the label value at position X is the one in the label stack value element that follows a position element containing X. That model was abandoned in favour of a long series of Information Elements, from mplsTopLabelStackSection through mplsLabelStackSection10, which removes the ambiguity but overloads the information model with repetitive information and would leave IANA unable to place a further element next to the others in the registry.
sections.plainLanguage: An IPFIX record lists values side by side, one after the other. That works for a single value of each kind, but not for a stack of labels or a group of attackers, where the same kind of value appears several times and the order matters. The old workarounds either flattened the structure, losing the relationships, or needed one template for every possible shape.

sections.title: The Three New Data Types
sections.content:
This document specifies three new abstract data types and three corresponding new Information Elements, called basicList, subTemplateList and subTemplateMultiList.

The type basicList represents a list of zero or more instances of any Information Element, primarily used for single-valued data types. Examples include a list of port numbers, a list of interface indexes, or a list of ASes in a BGP AS-PATH.

The type subTemplateList represents a list of zero or more instances of a structured data type, where the data type of each list element is the same and corresponds with a single Template Record. Examples include a structured data type composed of multiple pairs of label stack entry position and label stack value, a structured data type composed of performance metrics, and a structured data type composed of multiple pairs of IP address.

The type subTemplateMultiList represents a list of zero or more instances of a structured data type, where the data type of each list element can be different and corresponds with different Template definitions. An example is a structured data type composed of multiple access-list entries, where entries can be composed of different criteria types.

The document also specifies a new data type semantic, list, which represents an arbitrary-length sequence of zero or more structured data Information Elements, either composed of regular Information Elements or composed of data conforming to a Template Record. The three Structured Data Information Elements carry some semantic information so that the Collecting Process can understand the relationship between the different list elements. If a list is composed of the elements (A,B,C), the semantic expresses the relationship among A, B and C, regardless of whether they are individual elements or lists of elements.

Where the Information Elements and abstract data types of the information model represent single values, the new abstract data types are structural in nature and primarily contain references to other Information Elements and to Templates. By referencing other Information Elements and Templates from an Information Element's data content, it becomes possible to define complex data structures and to specify hierarchical containment relationships between Templates. For that reason the document prefers the more generic term Data Record to Flow Record.
sections.plainLanguage: Three new kinds of value are defined. One holds any number of plain values of the same kind. One holds any number of records that all follow the same template. One holds any number of records that may each follow a different template, so a list can mix shapes.

sections.title: The Semantics of a List
sections.content:
Structured data type semantics express the relationship among the multiple list elements in a Structured Data Information Element. They require a new IPFIX subregistry.

The undefined semantic, which is the default, says that the semantic of list elements is not specified and that, if a semantic exists, it is up to the Collecting Process to draw its own conclusions. A mediator translating plain IPFIX into structured data uses it, because plain IPFIX carries no semantic.

The noneOf semantic says that none of the elements are actual properties of the Data Record. A router monitoring specific BGP AS-PATHs would use it to report that a Flow belongs to none of the paths it watches.

The exactlyOneOf semantic says that only a single element from the structured data is an actual property of the Data Record, which is equivalent to a logical XOR operation. A basicList of outgoing interfaces with that semantic means the Flow egressed from a single interface, even though the record lists all the possible ones, which is a typical per-destination load balancing.

The oneOrMoreOf semantic says that one or more elements from the list are actual properties of the Data Record, equivalent to a logical OR operation.

The allOf semantic says that all of the list elements are actual properties of the Data Record. A basicList of outgoing interfaces with that semantic describes a multicast Flow where each packet was replicated to each outgoing interface in the list.

The ordered semantic says that elements from the list are ordered. An Exporter reporting the AS10 AS20 AS30 AS40 BGP AS-PATH would use a basicList of those four ASes with that semantic.
sections.plainLanguage: A list on its own does not say what the items mean. The semantics say: none of these apply, exactly one applies, at least one applies, all of them apply, or the order matters. Without one of these the collector has to guess.

sections.title: How the Lists Are Encoded
sections.content:
The basicList Information Element represents a list of zero or more instances of an Information Element. Its encoding begins with a Semantic field, which indicates the relationship among the different Information Element values within the structured data Information Element. Next comes the Field ID, the Information Element identifier of the Information Elements contained in the list. The Element Length field gives the length in octets of each list element, or holds 0xFFFF if the length is encoded as a variable-length Information Element at the start of the content. Effectively the Element Length field is part of the header, so even in the case of a zero-element list it MUST NOT be omitted. The basicList Content follows, and a Collecting Process decodes list elements from it until no further data remains; a field count is not included but can be derived when the Information Element is decoded.

The Field ID is shown with the Enterprise bit, the most significant bit, set to 0. If the Enterprise bit is set to 1, a four-byte Enterprise Number MUST be encoded immediately after the Element Length. If a basicList has zero elements, the encoded data contains the Semantic field, the Field ID, the Element Length field and the four-byte Enterprise Number if present, while the content is empty.

The subTemplateList Information Element represents a list of zero or more Data Records corresponding to a specific Template. Its encoding begins with the Semantic field and a Template ID. Because the Template Record referenced by a subTemplateList can itself contain other subTemplateList Information Elements, and because those Template Record references are part of the Information Element content in the Data Record, it is possible to represent complex hierarchical data structures.

The subTemplateMultiList Information Element represents a list of zero or more instances of a structured data type where each list element can have a different data type. Its content is a sequence of groups, each made of a Template ID, the total length of the Data Records encoding for that Template ID, and the Data Records themselves. A Collecting Process decodes the Data Records according to the Template Record until no further data remains, and further Template IDs and Data Records may then be decoded according to the overall subTemplateMultiList length. A record count is not included but can be derived, and encoding and decoding are performed recursively if the specified Template itself contains Structured Data Information Elements. In the exceptional case of zero instances, no data is encoded, only the Semantic field and the Template ID fields, and the Data Records Length field is set to zero.
sections.plainLanguage: Each list starts with a header that says what the items mean and how long each one is, and then the items follow. A list of records also names the template each group of records follows, so the collector knows how to read them.

sections.title: Lengths, Recursion and Padding
sections.content:
When the encoding of a Structured Data Information Element has a fixed length, because it contains the same number of fixed-length elements, or because the permutations of elements in the list always produce the same total length, the element length can be encoded in the corresponding Template Record.

When representing variable-length data, hierarchical data and repeated data with variable element counts, where the number and length of elements can vary from record to record, the RFC RECOMMENDS that the Information Elements are encoded using the variable-length encoding of section 7 of RFC 5101, with the length carried before the Structured Data Information Element encoding. Because of the complex and repeated nature of the data, it is potentially difficult for the Exporting Process to know the exact encoding size in advance, so the Exporting Process may encode the available data starting at a fixed offset and fill in the final length afterwards. The three-byte length encoding is therefore RECOMMENDED for variable-length Information Elements in all Template Records containing a Structured Data Information Element, even if the encoded length can be less than 255 bytes, because the starting offset of the data is known in advance. An Exporting Process MUST take care not to exceed the maximum allowed IPFIX message length of 65535 bytes.

Recursive relationships between structured data instances are possible, for example when representing a tree structure: a basicList where each element is itself a basicList, or a subTemplateList where one of the fields of the referenced Template is itself a subTemplateList referencing the same Template. The Exporting Process MUST take care when encoding recursively-defined structured data not to exceed the maximum allowed length of an IPFIX Message.

Structured Data Information Elements MAY be used in Options Template Sets, and, since the IPFIX specification does not prevent the use of any Information Element for scope, one MAY be used as scope in an Options Template Set. The Exporting Process MAY insert padding octets in structured data field values in a Data Record by including the paddingOctets Information Element, which can be included in a Template Record referenced by a structured data Information Element for this purpose.
sections.plainLanguage: Because a list can be any length, the exporter cannot always know in advance how big it will be, so the length is written after the data. The RFC asks for a three-byte length field so that the position of the data is known in advance and only the number has to be filled in later.

sections.title: Template Management and the Collecting Process
sections.content:
Template ID uniqueness is unchanged compared with RFC 5101: the uniqueness is local to the Transport Session and Observation Domain that generated the Template ID, and the Set ID used to export the Template Record does not influence it. The rule from RFC 5101 that, if an Information Element is required more than once in a Template, the different occurrences SHOULD follow the logical order of their treatment by the Metering Process, MAY be ignored within Structured Data Information Elements.

Templates that are not used anymore SHOULD be deleted. Deleting a Template implies that it MUST NOT be used within a subTemplateList or a subTemplateMultiList anymore, and before reusing a Template ID the Template MUST be deleted. A Template is withdrawn through the use of a Template Withdrawal Message.

On the collecting side, IPFIX Messages with Structured Data Information Elements change the IPFIX concept from the Collector's point of view, as the data types are present in the Data Records rather than in the Template Records. A basicList Information Element in a Template Record does not specify the list element data type; that information is in the Data Record, and in the case of a subTemplateMultiList the Collecting Process must refer to the included Template Records in the middle of the Data Record decode.

A Collecting Process MUST note the Information Element identifier of any Information Element it does not understand and MAY discard that Information Element. So a Collecting Process that does not support this extension can ignore the Structured Data Information Elements in a Data Record, or it can ignore Data Records containing them while continuing to process other Data Records. If the structured data carries the undefined semantic, the Collecting Process MAY attempt to draw its own conclusion about the semantic contained in the Data Record.
sections.plainLanguage: A collector that has never heard of this extension can still read the rest of the record: it notes the element it does not know and skips it. The type information now sits in the data rather than in the template, which is what makes that possible.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The addition of complex data types necessarily complicates the implementation of the Collector. This could easily result in new security vulnerabilities, such as buffer overflows, and it creates additional risk in cases where either Datagram Transport Layer Security is not used, or where the Observation Point and the Collector belong to different trust domains. Otherwise, the same security considerations as for the IPFIX protocol and the IPFIX information model apply.
sections.plainLanguage: More complicated data means more complicated code in the collector, and the RFC warns that this is where new bugs, such as buffer overflows, can appear. The risk is higher when the traffic is not protected or when the two ends do not trust each other.

viz.caption: THE THREE NEW ABSTRACT DATA TYPES

cells: Zero or more instances of any Information Element
Zero or more instances of one structured type, all from the same Template Record
Zero or more instances of structured types, each from a different Template Record

items.label: UNDEFINED
items.desc: The default. The meaning of the list elements is not specified.

items.label: NONE OF
items.desc: None of the elements are actual properties of the Data Record.

items.label: EXACTLY ONE OF
items.desc: Only a single element is an actual property of the Data Record.

items.label: ONE OR MORE OF
items.desc: One or more elements are actual properties of the Data Record.

items.label: ALL OF
items.desc: All of the list elements are actual properties of the Data Record.

items.label: ORDERED
items.desc: The elements from the list are ordered.

viz.caption: THE HEADER OF A basicList ELEMENT (RFC 6313)

fields.name: Semantic
fields.desc: The relationship among the list elements.

fields.name: Field ID
fields.desc: The Information Element identifier of the values in the list, with the Enterprise bit as its most significant bit.

fields.name: Element Length
fields.desc: The length in octets of each list element, or 0xFFFF when the length is variable. It is part of the header and must not be omitted.

A NESTED SEMANTIC EXAMPLE FROM RFC 6313

BGP AS-PATH = (basicList, ordered,

    (basicList, ordered, AS10,AS20,AS30,AS40),

    (basicList, exactlyOneOf, AS50, AS60)
